algorithm: Initialize a color array to track the bipartition of each vertex.
Perform a BFS or DFS traversal of the graph, assigning colors to vertices.
Check if any vertex has an adjacent vertex with the same color.
If no such pair exists, the graph is bipartite.
constraints: Edges must be distinct and valid (0 <= u < v < n).
The graph is simple and undirected.
Isolated vertices are allowed and considered bipartite.
The function returns a boolean value for predicates.
edge_cases: n = 2 (two vertices with no edge: bipartite)
n = 3 (three vertices with no edges: bipartite)
n = 3 (three vertices with one edge: bipartite)
n = 3 (three vertices with two edges: bipartite)
inputs: n is an integer >= 1; edges is a list of distinct [u, v] pairs with 0 <= u < v < n.
output: Returns True if the graph is bipartite, False otherwise.
purpose: Determines if a given graph is bipartite.
